body:
Afaik this should actually be safe to do here, instead of using a `Read` as in the old `PoolVector`.

The old version needed a `Read` because the memory pool could start compacting at any point, so raw pointers to `PoolVector` data weren't safe to use.

The new version uses a `LocalVector`, and no background process can relocate these allocations, only `resize`, `clear` etc can do this, and they will cause COW and create new data, therefore the read is still safe.

This makes access via this operator much faster in this new version.
I've actually changed this to `explicit` to match `LocalVector`, but will leave for the next push so as not to hammer CI.

Technically with this new PR, these no longer need to be lifetime bound, as the `Shared` will be preserved until the `Access` is destroyed (that was a bug with the old one, see #69804 ).

But it's neater if the compiler can still find these, as in most cases, it will not be what you wanted to do.

This (or similar) seems required to prevent warnings for possible overflow in `memcpy` by letting a negative signed `U` for count to creep in.

Ultimately I'm aiming to deprecate signed U / `LocalVectori` but that should be a separate PR because there are opportunities for bugs to creep in due to e.g. overflow in reverse iteration.

Also aiming to deprecate `force_trivial` now we have `resize_uninitialized()`, but again, for another PR.
